title: Context-generated plasticity rule coordinate
hypothesis: A compact context-conditioned coordinate on a shared secant-Hebbian update rule will improve few-step adaptation across task curvature regimes at no more serialized rule bytes or update compute than a generic context-to-learning-rate control.
mirror_coordinate: Scalar coordinate modulating the shared secant-estimated learning rate from online gradient history
logical_multiplicity: Task-adaptive update behavior across curvature regimes
controls: Mirror coordinate on shared secant rule
per-task best fixed rate diagnostic upper control

development.selection_metric: mean final quadratic excess loss after 12 updates

paid_objects: writable current parameters and gradient-history state

success_gate: Fresh final excess loss improves >=10% versus fixed-rate baseline while matching native context gate within 1% payload bytes and <=1.05x online MACs; for Mirror-specific claim additionally beat native context gate by >=5% loss at matched bytes/compute.
failure_gate: No quality improvement over fixed rate, or native context gate matches Mirror within 1% quality/bytes, or update compute exceeds 1.05x native control.
boundaries: Synthetic quadratic adaptation only; no learned optimizer or differentiable-plasticity training claim.
Development seed 17 selects fixed rate and shared rule multiplier; fresh seeds 37/59 are never tuned.
Task curvature information is available only through observed gradient history, not teacher Hessians at inference.
